part.text:
Now I understand the bug: in `decCompare` (src/decNumber/decNumber.c:6209), `rhs->exponent - lhs->exponent` can overflow `Int` (exponents range down to ~-2e9, up to ~1e9), producing a negative exponent passed to `decUnitCompare`, which then computes a negative `exprem` used to index `powers[]` → OOB read/segfault.

The fix: compute the difference safely (with `Long`) and short-circuit when the exponents are too far apart for the coefficients to ever make up the difference.

part.text:
Fixed. The root cause was in `decCompare` (src/decNumber/decNumber.c:6209): `rhs->exponent - lhs->exponent` overflows `Int` (int32) when exponents are far apart (e.g. `506760210 - -1999999996`), and the resulting negative value is passed to `decUnitCompare`, where `exp % DECDPUN` becomes a negative index into `powers[]` → OOB read/segfault.

The fix computes the exponent difference in 64-bit (`Long`) and short-circuits when the difference is >= the digits of the smaller-exponent coefficient — in that case `B*10^E >= 10^E > A`, so the comparison result is known without calling `decUnitCompare` (which also avoids pathological huge allocations for large-but-representable exponent gaps). In the remaining branch the difference fits in `Int`, so the subtraction is safe.

Verified:
- `./jq -n '3E506760210 < 63E-6855002263'` → `false`, `[ 3E506760210, 63E-6855002263 ] | sort` → works, plus sign/equality edge cases (`1E+999999999 == 1E+999999999`, negatives, extreme exponents) all correct.
- A standalone UBSan harness over `decNumberCompare` with extreme exponents reports no undefined behavior.
- `make check` in the testbed container: all 8 test suites pass.
